summary: A future held at Quote by one client and at Depth by another: the desktop subscribes the depth feed alone while Depth is held (the touchline goes) and both frames carry OI; once Depth is released the touchline comes back and the Quote frame carries the OI just sent.

notes: The desktop subscribes one effective mode per instrument (websocket::manager Entry::effective) and the feeds that mode needs (streaming.rs feeds, mode_change_frames); the web counts references per feed and keeps the touchline for the Quote client. The public frames do not depend on it: the depth feed carries every touchline field.

No frame carries the depth feed's `ltt` (an IST HH:MM:SS): the desktop reads it on the IST day the tick arrives (streaming.rs clock_on_day_of), so its epoch-ms value depends on the day the case runs and cannot be pinned here; brokers::definedge::tests::quote_feed::a_depth_message_carries_the_full_quote_and_the_trade_time pins it. Without it both sides take the feed time `ft` (epoch seconds) as the trade time.

deviations.reason: Definedge's web adapter sends ltq (its name for last_quantity) in Depth only (_DEPTH_EXTRA_FIELDS); the desktop's names table sends it from Quote. Phase B: from Depth, in Definedge's entry of feed/dialect/names.rs.

The web forwards Definedge's raw time as ltt: the feed time `ft` in epoch seconds (or the depth feed's clock text HH:MM:SS), a wrong value where feed timestamps are epoch milliseconds (docs/prompt/websockets-format.md); it is a JSON string as well. The desktop sends the epoch ms value.
The web sends the previous day's open interest (Definedge `poi`); the desktop's common carrier drops it.

deviations.reason: Definedge's web adapter sends the percent change only (change_percent, percent_change), never price_change, for any instrument; the desktop adds its canonical price_change. Lead rules 2026-11-09: change keys outside the docs follow the adapter; dropped in Phase B through the per-broker switch.

Definedge's web adapter names the percent change change_percent and percent_change (both sent by the desktop too); the desktop adds its canonical price_change_percent. Dropped in Phase B through the per-broker switch (lead rules 2026-11-09).
The web sends the total open interest (Definedge `toi`); the desktop's common carrier drops it.
